chapters.title: A family and a promise
chapters.place: Vermont and West Lebanon New Hampshire
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: Joseph was born on December 23, 1805, in Sharon, Vermont. A childhood illness led to surgery on his left leg while his family lived in New Hampshire. Family care, poverty, work, and vulnerability precede his public calling.
chapters.intro: Begin as the recovering boy, with a low eye height and a fully explorable small room. Reach for water, call for a parent, and accept help walking to the doorway. A short passage of seasons connects recovery to the family journey. The surgery stays off screen; the player experiences trust and care rather than a medical challenge.
chapters.epilogue: The hand offered to Joseph becomes the hand he offers to others throughout the campaign.

chapters.title: Many voices in Palmyra
chapters.status: Historical setting with composite townspeople
chapters.history: The Smith family moved to the Palmyra area in 1816. Joseph's account describes competing Methodist, Presbyterian, and Baptist claims. Freemasonry also belonged to the region's civic culture; this does not establish a town-wide conspiracy or a Masonic cause of his visions.
chapters.intro: Work a short farm route, enter three distinct preaching gatherings, and ask each minister a sincere question. Their responses reveal differing beliefs through human conversations. Pass an understated lodge notice as ordinary civic scenery. At home, open James 1:5 and choose a quiet place to seek God's guidance.
chapters.epilogue: The first essential action is listening. The desire for religious certainty becomes a personal prayer.

chapters.title: The Sacred Grove
chapters.status: Joseph Smith account presented as true within the game
chapters.history: In the canonical account, fourteen-year-old Joseph prays in the woods and sees God the Father and Jesus Christ. The game uses that account as its principal staging text. Other surviving accounts belong in the optional history journal without suggesting that one cinematic reconstruction is a camera record.
chapters.intro: Walk into the grove, choose where to kneel, and begin the prayer. The player participates in the moment of distress and appeal without a timed button test. Light enters the actual canopy; the Father and the Son are distinct embodied figures. Let the player look freely, stand in third person, or move the observation camera throughout the encounter. Return to the same ordinary trees afterward.
chapters.epilogue: The small clearing becomes the visual memory returned to in the last chapter.

chapters.title: Moroni in the night
chapters.status: Joseph Smith account presented devotionally
chapters.history: Joseph describes Moroni's repeated visits during the night, followed by a further encounter the next day. This happens after the First Vision. Moroni tells him about an ancient sacred record and his future responsibility.
chapters.intro: Retire to the attic bedroom, pray, awaken to the visitor, and listen. Repeated visits change the moonlight and the condition of the room subtly, rather than replaying a long identical speech. At morning work Joseph's exhaustion becomes embodied movement; speaking with his father opens the journey to the hill.
chapters.epilogue: The bedtime interior and the immense sacred history announced within it establish the game's contrast of ordinary life and eternity.

chapters.title: The hill and the years of preparation
chapters.place: The hill near Manchester and the Smith home
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: Joseph first sees the plates in 1823 but receives them in 1827, after years of preparation. His brother Alvin dies in November 1823. The narrative connects the family's bereavement with the later importance of salvation for the dead without inventing a revelation at Alvin's deathbed.
chapters.intro: Find the hill through landmarks, uncover the stone box, and obey the instruction to wait. Return on successive seasonal visits while doing farm and family tasks. Sit with the family after Alvin's death. The plate chamber is a custody encounter, not a treasure-looting reward.
chapters.epilogue: Waiting, restraint, and family love become playable virtues before public leadership.

chapters.title: Emma and the entrusted record
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: Joseph and Emma Hale marry on January 18, 1827. He obtains the plates on September 22 and moves to Harmony later that year. Emma is an active partner in the emerging work, not a companion whose only purpose is admiration.
chapters.intro: A brief courtship conversation leads to the marriage and a dated transition. Prepare the wagon with Emma, retrieve and wrap the record, secure it, and travel through a dangerous route. Protection means finding shelter, listening for pursuers, and trusting helpers. The player can inspect the weight and handling of the wrapped plates without turning them into a weapon or inventory currency.
chapters.epilogue: The private commitment to Emma and the public responsibility for the record enter the same story.

chapters.title: Harmony and the lost manuscript
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: Emma and Martin Harris assist the early translation. Martin's entrusted manuscript of 116 pages is lost in 1828. That year also brings the death of Joseph and Emma's first child and Emma's serious illness. Repentance and care belong beside the loss of the pages.
chapters.intro: Prepare a quiet workspace, listen to Emma, dictate short reviewed passages, and arrange ordinary household tasks around translation. Martin requests the manuscript; the event follows the historical outcome. When he returns, the player must face the loss, comfort Emma, and seek forgiveness. There is no alternate branch where perfect button timing recovers the pages.
chapters.epilogue: Calling does not remove grief or the need to learn responsibility.

chapters.title: Oliver and the work of translation
chapters.place: Harmony and the Whitmer farm in Fayette
chapters.status: Devotional reconstruction based on translation accounts
chapters.history: Oliver Cowdery becomes the principal scribe in 1829. Church sources discuss both the interpreters and a seer stone, including use of a hat to exclude light. The precise phenomenology of revelation is not documented in a way that fixes every visible detail.
chapters.intro: Welcome Oliver, arrange the desk, dictate selected text, listen to read-back, and continue after interruptions. Include a historically grounded seer-stone-and-hat setup, alongside appropriate coverage of the interpreters. Faithfulness means receiving scripture through God's gift, not solving invented ancient-language puzzles or choosing which doctrine the book will contain. Move the household to Fayette through a dated chapter transition.
chapters.epilogue: The ordinary sound of a spoken sentence becoming a written line is the central miracle of the chapter.

chapters.title: Authority beside the river
chapters.status: Faithful presentation with dating limits preserved
chapters.history: John the Baptist's appearance and the mutual baptisms of Joseph and Oliver are associated with May 15, 1829. Peter, James, and John also restore priesthood authority in the Church's account. The exact date of that latter encounter should not be invented or presented as established.
chapters.intro: Leave the desk because a question about baptism demands prayer. Kneel with Oliver, receive the angelic visitation, enter the river, and participate in the baptisms with deliberate contextual actions. A separate encounter presents the apostles. The player enacts preparation and participation; sacred authority never becomes a rechargeable spell system.
chapters.epilogue: The record leads to an organized covenant community, not merely to private mystical experiences.

chapters.title: Witnesses and the printed book
chapters.status: Distinct historical witness events
chapters.history: The Three Witnesses and the Eight Witnesses give different kinds of testimony and should have separate scenes. Printing follows at E. B. Grandin's establishment. Martin Harris's financial sacrifice is part of bringing the book to readers.
chapters.intro: Pray with the Three Witnesses in an angelic encounter, then host the separate handling of the plates by the Eight. Travel to the print shop, inspect a composed page, help carry sheets, and place the finished book into another person's hands. None of the player-controlled printing tasks lets a typo rewrite scripture.
chapters.epilogue: Private reception becomes public testimony and a durable physical book.

chapters.title: The Church and the first New York congregations
chapters.place: Fayette Colesville and the New York settlements
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: The Church is organized on April 6, 1830. Early preaching, baptisms, opposition, and arrests accompany its growth. The initial organization is the Church of Christ; the present full Church name belongs to the later naming history. Emma's call and hymn work deserve a visible place.
chapters.intro: Prepare the room, welcome families, participate in sustaining and sacramental worship, and visit people who have questions. Preach to a small audience using reviewed sermon beats. Walk with Emma after baptism amid hostility and help her plan a hymn collection. An early arrest is a short experience of uncertainty and support, distinct from the final Carthage arrest.
chapters.epilogue: Zion begins as actual people agreeing to care for one another.

chapters.title: Gathering to Ohio
chapters.status: Historical devotional dramatization
chapters.history: The Church gathers to Kirtland in 1831, an essential stage between New York and Joseph's later Missouri residence. Newel K. Whitney's store and a growing community provide a setting for questions about stewardship, resources, and shared life.
chapters.intro: Arrive with Emma, meet Whitney, find housing for newcomers, and assist a family with few supplies. Participate in a council about consecration through concrete choices about food, work, land, and fair treatment. A city plan appears as an achievable shared task rather than a magic construction menu.
chapters.epilogue: Gathering requires an economy of care, not only a powerful sermon.
